title: Pong was not the first home video game.
description:
Pong was not the first home video game. A defence engineer in New Hampshire built a multi-game TV console years before Atari.

Engineer at Sanders Associates in Nashua, New Hampshire. He began work on games that plug into a television.

The Brown Box had a light gun and a golf putter. Its seventh version, TV Game Unit #7, was wrapped in brown wood-grain vinyl to look more appealing to investors.

Nolan Bushnell saw the Odyssey demonstration. Atari's Pong followed. Magnavox and Sanders later sued Atari, and Atari settled and became a licensee.

Baer's figure for Odyssey sales between 1972 and 1975, at $99.95 each.

The patent fights around it paid out more than $100 million.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnavox_Odyssey - Wikipedia; established the Brown Box as the seventh prototype finished in January 1969, the Sanders and Magnavox agreement signed in January 1971, the September 1972 North American release at $99.95, 28 games across 11 game cards, Baer's figure of 350,000 units sold before discontinuation in 1975, Bushnell seeing a demonstration in May 1972, and more than $100 million won in patent suits and settlements.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_H._Baer - Wikipedia; established Baer's employer Sanders Associates in Nashua, New Hampshire, the team of Bill Harrison and Bill Rusch, U.S. Patent 3,728,480 granted 17 April 1973, and Baer's dispute with Bushnell over credit.
- https://si.edu/es/object/brown-box-1967-68%3Anmah_1301997 - Smithsonian National Museum of American History catalogue entry; established the prototype as TV Game Unit #7, nicknamed for its brown wood-grain vinyl, with two controllers, multiple games including ping-pong, a light gun and golf putting.
- https://www.history.com/articles/brown-box-home-gaming-ralph-baer - History.com; independently confirmed the 1971 Magnavox licence, the 1972 release at $99.95, 350,000 units sold from 1972 to 1975, Bushnell's 1972 sight of the table tennis demo, and that Atari later settled the patent suit and became a licensee.
